title: Unit – 1 : Session – 5 : SLO – 2  |  Signed magnitude subtraction
sections: 2. b — -2 ((+3)-(+5): smaller minus larger → negative, magnitude 5-3=2)
3. c — (+A) - (-B) (becomes addition of magnitudes, which can overflow)
4. b — +2 ((-3)-(-5) = +2: magnitudes 5-3=2, sign of larger magnitude operand is +)

1. (+A)-(-B) and (-A)-(+B) turn into magnitude ADDITION (subtracting a negative). The result magnitude A+B can exceed the (N-1)-bit magnitude field (e.g. 5+3=8 > 7 in 4-bit), so the true result cannot be represented — overflow.

2. Same-sign subtraction steps: (i) compare magnitudes; (ii) subtract the smaller magnitude from the larger; (iii) keep the common sign if the first operand's magnitude is larger, otherwise take the opposite sign; (iv) if magnitudes are equal the result is +0.
(-5) - (+3): different signs → this becomes magnitude addition: 5 + 3 = 8, and the sign of the result is the sign of the first operand (negative) → true result -8.
Step-by-step: -5 = 1101, +3 = 0011. Magnitudes 101 + 011 = 1000 (8). Magnitude field is 3 bits (max 111 = 7). 8 > 7 → magnitude cannot fit.
OVERFLOW occurs: -8 is outside the 4-bit signed magnitude range (-7 to +7).
E. 4-bit signed magnitude — 5. Range from -7 to +7

(+5) - (+3): both positive. Compare magnitudes: 101 > 011. Subtract: 101 - 011 = 010 (2). Sign stays positive.
